div.head: Northu 50
div.ab: Gif hit si færbena, gilde XII ór.
Gif hit si færbena, gilde XII or.
Wenn es ein gemeinfreier Hintersasse(?) ist, zahle er 12 Ör.
If it is a common freeman tenant(?), let him pay 12 ores.
If it is færbena, he is to pay 12 ores.
If he is a commoner, he is to pay twelve oras.
div.note: Apparently the same as the cyrlisc man of chap. 53, the tunesman “villager” of chap. 59, and the ceorl of chap. 60. It must denote a freeman who is not a landowner. By etymology, it should mean “journey-petitioner” and the interpretation in Bosworth-Toller, Supplement, “one who has to ask leave to go from his lord”, which is equivalent to the Domesday Book “could not recede”, seems preferable to Liebermann's interpretation, “one who claims the right to go”, i.e. a higher class of tenant, for this forces the meaning of bena, “a suppliant”. Færbenu glosses epifates, “passengers”, “those who request a passage” in the Erfurt Glossary, which is not very helpful.

commoner: The term used here is færbena, a word of uncertain meaning. The similar penalty for wrongdoing indicates that the færbena is equal in status to the cyrlisc man (commoner) and ceorl (peasant) of clauses 53 and 60 and the tunes man (townsman) of clause 59; however, the precise nature of his obligations to his lord remains unclear.
